$comment: Published examination schedule for GATE 2027, the examination cycle the
bundled GATE CSE curriculum is transcribed from.
Source: the GATE 2027 website published by IIT Madras, the organising
institute -- https://gate2027.iitm.ac.in/ -- recorded in `source_reference`
below and read on the date in `source_checked_on`. Every date below was
verified against that source on 2026-08-01.
`schedule_status` is `provisional`, and must stay so until the organising
institute confirms the dates. The source states that every date it publishes
is liable to change, and a schedule stored without that qualification would
read as settled fact in every plan built against it.
Transcription rules, applied uniformly so the file stays checkable against
the source:
* One period per published date or date range. A period that occupies a
single day repeats that day in `starts_on` and `ends_on`.
* The three examination weekends are three separate `examination` periods,
not one 6-21 February range. The weekdays between them are not sitting
days, and spanning them would put eleven days into the examination
window that no examination occupies.
* No period names the day the Computer Science paper itself is sat. The
organising institute has not published it. The examination window is what
is known; a single CS date would be a guess presented as a deadline.
* `results` is the announcement day, 19 March 2027.
One inference, recorded because the source does not state it directly:
* The source publishes closing dates for registration -- 21 September 2026
at the regular fee, 30 September 2026 with the late fee -- rather than an
opening date for the late period. `late_registration` is therefore
recorded as beginning the day after regular registration closes, which is
the only reading consistent with both published dates. If the institute
later publishes an explicit opening date, correct this entry and re-run
the seed; it updates the period in place.
name: GATE 2027
